Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A. 
Hon'ble Saurabh Shyam Shamshery,J. 
1. Heard Sri Satyendra Narayan Singh, learned counsel for applicant and Sri Paritosh Malviya,
learned A.G.A. appearing on behalf of State.

2. Applicant- Anas, has approached this Court by way of filing the present Criminal Misc. Bail Application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. in Case Crime No.77 of 2022 under Sections 363, 366, 376(3)
I.P.C. and 5/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station- Charthawal, District - Muzaffar Nagar after rejection of his Bail Application vide order dated 06.02.2023 passed by Additional District and Sessions Judge/Special Judge(POCSO Act), Muzaffar Nagar.

3. According to contents of First Information Report, informant(father of victim) lodged an F.I.R.
against two named accused and one unknown, including applicant herein that they have entices her minor daughter, aged about 15 years, and kept her away from his lawful guardianship with intention to compel her for marriage.

His minor girl has taken some gold and silver jewellery items along with Anas vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163131612/

sentences.text: her. F.I.R. was lodged on 23.03.2022.
4. Learned counsel for applicant has submitted that victim was recovered on 12.12.2022(after eight and a half months).

Thereafter, her statements were recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
that she left her home on her own will, however, nature of allegations in regard to applicant and co-accused were contrary in both the statements.

5. Learned counsel for applicant has referred statement victim under Section 161 Cr.P.C. wherein she has made main allegations against applicant that she lived with him as husband-wife for about eight months and they had physical relationship also.

In this statement she has not made any specific allegation of rape against co-accused Aris, however, she took a somersault in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. wherein main allegation of rape and living together was alleged on co-accused Aris, whereas allegations against present applicant were limited that she remained with him only for few days and no specific allegation was made in regard to any physical relationship with him.
6.

Learned counsel for applicant has referred statements mainly, the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and submits that since there was no allegation of rape of victim against applicant and evidence in regard to offence under Sections 363 and 366 I.P.C. appears to be very weak,
therefore, applicant who is in jail since 21.12.2022 be released on bail and in case, he is released on bail, he shall not misuse liberty of bail and will cooperate in trial also.

7. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail and submitted that version of victim remained consistent in both above referred statements that applicant was involved in enticing her and committing offence of kidnapping from a lawful guardianship.
She also remained consistent that she stayed along with applicant also.

She has not made any specific allegation of rape in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., against applicant, however, at this stage, it cannot be ruled out that when victim was staying with applicant even for a short period, she never get into physical relationship with him as well as she has not denied any physical relationship with applicant, though in statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. she has made specific allegation of rape against applicant.
8. LAW ON BAIL - A SUMMARY (A) The basic rule may perhaps be tersely put as bail, not jail.

(B) Power to grant bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C., is of wide amplitude but not an unfettered discretion, which calls for exercise in a judicious manner and not as a matter of course or in whimsical manner.

(C) While passing an order on an application for grant of bail, there is no need to record elaborate details to give an impression that the case is one that would result in a conviction or, by contrast, in an acquittal.

sentences.text: The Court may also take note of participation or part of an unlawful assembly as well as that circumstantial evidence not being a ground to grant bail, if the evidence/ material collected establishes prima facie a complete chain of events.
Parity may not be an only ground but remains a relevant factor for consideration of application for bail.

(D) Over crowding of jail and gross delay in disposal of cases when undertrials are forced to remain in jail (not due to their fault) may give rise to possible situations that may justify invocation of Article 21 of Constitution, may also be considered along with other factors.

sentences.text: In the present case, victim is a minor girl.

There is a merit in the argument of learned counsel for applicant that though specific allegations of physical relationship were made against him and consent being of a minor is immaterial, therefore, according to statement of victim under Section 161 Cr.P.C. an offence of rape is made out, however, in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. an absolutely contrary version was taken and as per her statement, applicant got scot free from the offence of rape, whereas entire allegations were levelled against co-accused and since at this stage, statement recorded before Magistrate under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has more persuasive value, therefore, prima facie no case is made out against applicant for making physical relationship with a minor girl with or without her consent, therefore, applicant who is in jail since 21.12.2022,
has made out a case of bail.
10. Trial Court is directed to record the statement of victim expeditiously preferably within a period of three months from today.
Applicant shall not enter within the boundaries of District-Muzaffar Nagar in the aforesaid period except for the purpose of present case or with prior permission from the Court.

11. Let the applicant- Anas be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.

3

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment or exemption from appearance on the date fixed in trial.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iii) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.
(iv) The Trial Court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously, preferably within a period of six months after release of applicant,
if there is no other legal impediment.

12. The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
The bail application is allowed.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
She has not made any specific allegation of rape in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., against applicant, however, at this stage, it cannot be ruled out that when victim was staying with applicant even for a short period, she never get into physical relationship with him as well as she has not denied any physical relationship with applicant, though in statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. she has made specific allegation of rape against applicant.
(B) Power to grant bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C., is of wide amplitude but not an unfettered discretion, which calls for exercise in a judicious manner and not as a matter of course or in whimsical manner.
(C) While passing an order on an application for grant of bail, there is no need to record elaborate details to give an impression that the case is one that would result in a conviction or, by contrast, in an acquittal.
However, a Court cannot completely divorce its decision from material aspects of the case such as allegations made against accused; nature and gravity of accusation; having common object or intention; severity of punishment if allegations are proved beyond reasonable doubt and would result in a conviction; reasonable apprehension of witnesses being influenced by accused;
tampering of evidence; character, behaviour, means, position and standing of accused; likelihood of Anas vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163131612/
2 offence being repeated; the frivolity in the case of prosecution; criminal antecedents of accused and a prima facie satisfaction of Court in support of charge against accused.
The Court may also take note of participation or part of an unlawful assembly as well as that circumstantial evidence not being a ground to grant bail, if the evidence/ material collected establishes prima facie a complete chain of events.
Parity may not be an only ground but remains a relevant factor for consideration of application for bail.
(D) Over crowding of jail and gross delay in disposal of cases when undertrials are forced to remain in jail (not due to their fault) may give rise to possible situations that may justify invocation of Article 21 of Constitution, may also be considered along with other factors.
